title: Disentangled Skill Representations for Predictive Human Modeling
abstract: arXiv:2608.23776v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Understanding human skill is important for AI systems that collaborate with, coach, or assist people. Unlike typical latent variable estimation problems which rely on single observations, skill is a persistent, compositional, and behaviorally grounded construct that must be inferred from patterns over time. We introduce Skill Abstraction with Interpretable Latents (SAIL), a method for modeling human skill as an interpretable, multi-dimensional construct inferred from naturalistic behavior. Furthermore, SAIL supports skill-informed behavior prediction that generalizes across a variety of in-domain contexts. translated_title: 解缠技能表征用于预测性人类建模
translated_abstract: 理解人类技能对于与人类协作、指导或辅助的AI系统非常重要。与依赖单一观测的典型潜在变量估计问题不同，技能是一种持久、组合且基于行为的构造，必须从随时间变化的模式中推断出来。我们引入了具有可解释潜在变量的技能抽象方法（SAIL），这是一种将人类技能建模为从自然行为中推断出的可解释、多维构造的方法。我们的方法产生了一种对瞬时表现波动具有鲁棒性的技能嵌入，并学习人类子技能的可迁移表征。此外，SAIL支持技能感知的行为预测，能泛化到各种领域内情境。我们用每个个体的持久技能嵌入来表示他们，该嵌入控制专家和新手基元之间的混合，并通过反事实子技能交换进行训练以实现解缠。
tldr: 本文提出了SAIL方法，通过解缠的可解释技能表征和反事实子技能交换，实现对人类技能的鲁棒建模和跨情境行为预测。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces SAIL, which models human skills via disentangled interpretable representations and counterfactual subskill swaps, enabling robust skill modeling and behavior prediction across contexts.
